verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）耶和华啊，我的心仰望你。
verses.en: By David.O Lord, I come before you in prayer.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 25. The psalmist asks for divine protection, guidance and forgiveness as he affirms his loyalty to and trust in the Lord. This psalm is an acrostic; every verse begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet, except for v. 18, which, like v. 19, begins with ר (resh) instead of the expected ק (qof). The final verse, which begins with פ (pe), stands outside the acrostic scheme.

verses.zh: 我的　神啊，我素来倚靠你；求你不要叫我羞愧，不要叫我的仇敌向我夸胜。
verses.en: My God, I trust in you.Please do not let me be humiliated;do not let my enemies triumphantly rejoice over me.

verses.zh: 凡等候你的必不羞愧；惟有那无故行奸诈的必要羞愧。
verses.en: Certainly none who rely on you will be humiliated.Those who deal in treachery will be thwarted[NOTE:1] and humiliated.
notes: Heb “to you, O Lord, my life I lift up.” To “lift up” one’s “life” to the Lord means to express one’s trust in him through prayer. See Pss 86:4; 143:8.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你将你的道指示我，将你的路教训我！
verses.en: Make me understand your ways, O Lord.Teach me your paths.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “those who deal in treachery in vain.” The adverb רֵיקָם (reqam, “in vain”) probably refers to the failure (or futility) of their efforts. Another option is to understand it as meaning “without cause” (cf. NIV84 “without excuse”; NIV11 “without cause”; NRSV “wantonly treacherous”).

verses.zh: 求你以你的真理引导我，教训我，因为你是救我的　神。我终日等候你。
verses.en: Guide me into your truth[NOTE:1] and teach me.For you are the God who delivers me;on you I rely all day long.
notes: Teach me your paths. In this context the Lord’s “ways” and “paths” refer to the moral principles which the Lord prescribes for his followers. See vv. 8-10.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你记念你的怜悯和慈爱，因为这是亘古以来所常有的。
verses.en: Remember[NOTE:1] your compassionate and faithful deeds, O Lord,for you have always acted in this manner.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Lord’s commandments are referred to as truth here because they are a trustworthy and accurate expression of the divine will.
That is, “remember” with the intention of repeating.

verses.zh: 求你不要记念我幼年的罪愆和我的过犯；耶和华啊，求你因你的恩惠，按你的慈爱记念我。
verses.en: Do not hold against me[NOTE:1] the sins of my youth[NOTE:2] or my rebellious acts.Because you are faithful to me, extend to me your favor, O Lord.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “for from antiquity [are] they.”
Heb “do not remember,” with the intention of punishing.
That is, the sins characteristic of youths, who lack moral discretion and wisdom.

verses.zh: 耶和华是良善正直的，所以他必指示罪人走正路。
verses.en: The Lord is both kind and fair;[NOTE:1] that is why he teaches sinners the right way to live.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “according to your faithfulness, remember me, you, for the sake of your goodness, O Lord.”
Heb “good and just.”

verses.zh: 他必按公平引领谦卑人，将他的道教训他们。
verses.en: May he show[NOTE:1] the humble what is right.[NOTE:2] May he teach[NOTE:3] the humble his way.
notes: Heb “teaches sinners in the way.”
The prefixed verbal form is jussive; the psalmist expresses his prayer.

Heb “may he guide the humble into justice.” The Hebrew term עֲנָוִים (ʿanavim, “humble”) usually refers to the oppressed, but in this context, where the psalmist confesses his sin and asks for moral guidance, it apparently refers to sinners who humble themselves before God and seek deliverance from their sinful condition.

verses.zh: 凡遵守他的约和他法度的人，耶和华都以慈爱诚实待他。
verses.en: The Lord always proves faithful and reliable[NOTE:1] to those who follow the demands of his covenant.[NOTE:2]
notes: The prefixed verbal form is interpreted as a jussive (it stands parallel to the jussive form, “may he guide”).
Heb “all the paths of the Lord are faithful and trustworthy.” The Lord’s “paths” refer here to his characteristic actions.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你因你的名赦免我的罪，因为我的罪重大。
verses.en: For the sake of your reputation,[NOTE:1] O Lord,forgive my sin, because it is great.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to the ones who keep his covenant and his testimonies.”
Heb “name.” By forgiving the sinful psalmist, the Lord’s reputation as a merciful God will be enhanced.

verses.zh: 谁敬畏耶和华，耶和华必指示他当选择的道路。
verses.en: The Lord shows his faithful followersthe way they should live.[NOTE:1]
notes: Forgive my sin because it is great. The psalmist readily admits his desperate need for forgiveness.

verses.zh: 他必安然居住；他的后裔必承受地土。
verses.en: They experience his favor;[NOTE:1] their descendants[NOTE:2] inherit the land.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Who is this man, the one who fears the Lord? He will instruct him in the way he should choose.” The singular (note “man”) is representative here (see v. 14, where the plural is used), and has thus been translated as a plural (“followers…they”).
Heb “his life in goodness dwells.” The singular is representative (see v. 14).
Or “offspring”; Heb “seed.”

verses.zh: 耶和华与敬畏他的人亲密；他必将自己的约指示他们。
verses.en: The Lord’s loyal followers receive his guidance,[NOTE:1] and he reveals his covenantal demands to them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “earth.”
Heb “the advice of the Lord belongs to those who fear him.”

verses.zh: 我的眼目时常仰望耶和华，因为他必将我的脚从网里拉出来。
verses.en: I continually look to the Lord for help,[NOTE:1] for he will free my feet from the enemy’s net.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and his covenant, to make them know.”
Heb “my eyes continually [are] toward the Lord.”

verses.zh: 求你转向我，怜恤我，因为我是孤独困苦。
verses.en: Turn toward me and have mercy on me,for I am alone[NOTE:1] and oppressed.
notes: Heb “for he will bring out from a net my feet.” The hostility of the psalmist’s enemies is probably in view (see v. 19).

verses.zh: 我心里的愁苦甚多，求你救我脱离我的祸患。
verses.en: Deliver me from my distress;[NOTE:1] rescue me from my suffering.[NOTE:2]
notes: That is, helpless and vulnerable.

Heb “the distresses of my heart, they make wide.” The text makes little if any sense as it stands, unless this is an otherwise unattested intransitive use of the Hiphil of רָחַב (rakhav, “be wide”). It is preferable to emend the form הִרְחִיבוּ (hirkhivu; Hiphil perfect third plural “they make wide”) to הַרְחֵיב (harkhev; Hiphil imperative masculine singular “make wide”). (The final vav [ו] can be joined to the following word and taken as a conjunction.) In this case one can translate, “[in/from] the distresses of my heart, make wide [a place for me],” that is, “deliver me from the distress I am experiencing.” For the expression “make wide [a place for me],” see Ps 4:1.

verses.zh: 求你看顾我的困苦，我的艰难，赦免我一切的罪。
verses.en: See my pain and suffering.Forgive all my sins.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “from my distresses lead me out.”

verses.zh: 求你察看我的仇敌，因为他们人多，并且痛痛地恨我。
verses.en: Watch my enemies, for they outnumber me;they hate me and want to harm me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “lift up all my sins.”

verses.zh: 求你保护我的性命，搭救我，使我不致羞愧，因为我投靠你。
verses.en: Protect me[NOTE:1] and deliver me!Please do not let me be humiliated,for I have taken shelter in you.
notes: Heb “see my enemies for they are numerous, and [with] violent hatred they hate me.”

verses.zh: 愿纯全、正直保守我，因为我等候你。
verses.en: May integrity and godliness protect me,for I rely on you.

verses.zh: 神啊，求你救赎以色列脱离他一切的愁苦。
verses.en: O God, rescue[NOTE:1] Israelfrom all their distress![NOTE:2]
notes: Or “my life.”
Or “redeem.”
